name: Congenital High-Molecular-Weight Kininogen Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Laboratory-based diagnostic criteria for HMWK deficiency

criteria.description: Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) not corrected by mixing studies
Normal factor XII activity to exclude factor XII deficiency
Markedly reduced or absent high-molecular-weight kininogen levels detected by specific assays
Lack of clinically significant bleeding despite coagulation abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of prolonged aPTT uncorrected by mixing studies, normal factor XII activity, and confirmed low or absent HMWK levels
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on specialized coagulation testing and exclusion of other contact factor deficiencies.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic laboratory finding without clinical bleeding tendency
searchTerms: delayed clotting time in lab test

pathognomonic.symptomName: Markedly reduced plasma high-molecular-weight kininogen levels
searchTerms: very low levels of plasma kininogen

common.notes: Most patients do not exhibit bleeding symptoms

searchTerms: slow clot formation in lab tests
mild bleeding from skin and mucous membranes

occasional.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding after trauma or surgery

occasional.notes: Rarely associated due to kininogen role in bradykinin generation

rare.symptomName: Hypotension episodes related to bradykinin deficiency
searchTerms: low blood pressure episodes from bradykinin deficiency
blood pressure drops due to bradykinin lack

laboratory: Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) uncorrected by mixing studies
Markedly decreased or absent high-molecular-weight kininogen levels
Normal factor XII and prekallikrein activity
other: No significant bleeding diathesis despite coagulation abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Prekallikrein deficiency shows prolonged aPTT corrected by mixing studies
Low prekallikrein levels instead of low HMWK
Factor XII deficiency presents with prolonged aPTT but normal HMWK levels

redFlags: Unexpected prolonged aPTT without bleeding symptoms
Failure to correct aPTT with mixing studies
references: Orphanet: Congenital High-Molecular-Weight Kininogen Deficiency - ORPHA:483
Mannucci PM, et al. High-molecular-weight kininogen deficiency: clinical and laboratory features. Haemophilia. 2004.
Fitzgerald Factor Deficiency. In: Hemostasis and Thrombosis: Basic Principles and Clinical Practice. 7th ed. 2013.
